# Games on Deck

*Page PDF 16*

THE CORSAIRS OF CAPTAIN FL ARIEL 

## **Games on Deck Medium Encounter**
If the Characters are at sea or at anchor in a remote location, you can challenge the party with this encounter, which involves a boarding action demonstrating the fickle temperament of Flariel and his corsairs. It is only suitable for Characters in ships smaller or similar size to the _Raptor’s Talon_ . 

The _Raptor’s Talon_ can close extremely quickly with enemy vessels, preferring to sweep in under cover of night, using Rakaria’s Illusion spell to conjure a ‘sea mist’ to conceal the approach. 

If all goes to plan, the Druchii ship moves in with disarming swiftness. She emerges from the mist alongside the Characters’ vessel, as two Ship’s Crew fire reapers to clear the decks of defenders. Captain Flariel leads a boarding party with 10 corsairs, firing crossbow pistols before engaging with their swords. Should they eliminate or incapacitate resistance, the Dark Elves do not slaughter all on board — Flariel is in the mood for entertainment tonight, so he demands an audience with the ship’s captain. 

Captain Flariel wishes to toy with his prey. He proposes a 

competition between his crew and the Characters. If they win two out of three games, he will leave everyone unharmed. If they lose, the Reavers will sacrifice half the crew to Mathlann and the remainder must serve in Naggaroth until they die. Flariel proposes three contests: 

- A duel between one of the corsairs and the party’s chosen champion. This is a single combat within a chalk circle drawn on the deck. The winner is whoever kills or incapacitates the opposition. If the corsair loses and survives, Flariel cuts their throat. He cordially congratulates the winner. 

- A contest of agility. Two nominated contenders must climb the main mast on the Characters’ ship and place a scrap of coloured cloth at the top. Flariel nominates one of his Lookouts to compete with whoever the Characters choose. Use the rules on page 165 of the **WFRP Core Rulebook** to determine who ascends fastest; whoever climbs 30 yards first wins. Combat at altitude is not against the rules… 

- A contest of artistry. Flariel states his kind are cultured folk, who enjoy the finer arts. The Characters’ contender must put on a performance — playing an instrument or “performing an act from one of those Tarradasch dramas we’ve heard so much about”. However, the Corsairs insist on the use of grisly props for the performance, such as real blood, a costume of flayed skin, or a musical instrument made from a skull and bones. Flariel selects one of his sailors (Ship’s Crew), who plays a mournful dirge on a conch shell wrapped in tatters of skin and sinew. This is an **Opposed Perform/Play** Test — with the winner judged by Flariel. He will concede if his contender loses, informing everyone that only a barbarian would cheat at such a contest. 

If the Characters propose alternative contests, Flariel assents if he believes victory is possible. While the games distract everyone, a Dark Elf Lookout sneaks below decks to drop a vial of Mandrake Root extract (see page 306 of the **WFRP Core Rulebook** ) into the ship’s fresh water barrels — insurance should Flariel’s crew lose the competition. Characters should have a chance to see this if they are vigilant. 

If the crew of the _Raptor’s Talon_ triumph, they attempt to take the crew prisoner, kill half, and steal all valuables. If they lose, they graciously return to the Raptor’s Talon, intending to return once the Mandrake Root takes effect. 

The boarding party consists of: 

- Captain Flariel. 

- 12 Dark Elf Corsairs. 

- 2 Corsairs providing supporting fire from reapers aboard the Raptor’s Talon.
